tei:bibl.tei:title: Differences from the 1822 Heidenheim original
tei:bibl.tei:note: (1) Biblical quotations in this edition were taken from the Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC), not from the printed 1822 haggadah text. (2) The original edition's ritual instructions, partly in German (in Hebrew characters) and partly in Hebrew, are not transcribed in the Hebrew project; English instructions appear only in the separate Feinstein translation project. (3) Heidenheim's edition notes and commentary are omitted. (4) The Ashkenazi German translation that accompanied the original Hebrew is not included. (5) Typography and layout follow modern digital conventions. Every page of the original is marked by a tei:pb milestone, placed at the exact point the page turns and verified page by page against the facsimile; folio 4v is the one page with nothing transcribed on it, carrying only Heidenheim's preface to Magid, so its milestone stands at the start of the next transcribed section. (6) Pre-seder material (bedikat chametz, biur chametz, eruv tavshilin) follows the Open Siddur compilation and may differ in scope or placement from the 1822 book. (7) Vocalization and spelling follow the Open Siddur transcription, not 1822 printing conventions. (8) The order of the concluding sections follows the 1822 print rather than the Open Siddur compilation. On folio 38r the print reads: Ki Lo Na'eh, לשנה הבאה בירושלים, the two fourth-cup blessings, then נרצה/Chasal Siddur Pesach — so the fourth-cup blessings are held back from Hallel to there, לשנה הבאה is separated from Chasal Siddur Pesach although the compilation runs them together, and Chasal Siddur Pesach follows rather than precedes the concluding piyyutim. Sefirat HaOmer stands between Adir Hu and Echad Mi Yodea (folio 39r). (9) Sections that are complete biblical units — Psalms 113 and 114 in Magid, 115, 116, 117, 118 and 136 in Hallel, and 126 in Barech — are separate documents carrying chapter and verse milestones with canonical biblical URNs, so they can be aligned with other witnesses. Their pointed text is the Westminster Leningrad Codex, as each records in its own tei:sourceDesc, and differs from the 1822 print in a handful of letters.
